landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District, 600 Sherbourne St, Leavenworth WA 98826 — (509) 548-2550. The summit, Lake Valhalla and the whole approach above the trailhead lie inside the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness. (The peak is sometimes mistakenly assigned to the Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest; the mountain is east of the crest, in the Okanogan-Wenatchee.)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful recommended (see fees — the Forest Service lists the site as no-fee, but a pass is also reported to be required).
drive: From the Old Lake Valhalla/Lake Janus Trailhead on Smith Brook Road (~4,150 ft)

names: NF-38 (Forest Service Road 38) / Middle Fork Nooksack
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From SR-542 about 3 miles east of Deming, turn right onto Mosquito Lake Road, go 4.8 miles, then turn left onto Middle Fork Road (FR-38) and follow it about 12.3 miles to where the road begins switchbacking uphill; park there, or sooner if snow stops you. Since July 2026 Forest Road 38 has been closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 7.

landManager: National Park Service
storedPass: Not a Northwest Forest Pass (that's a USFS pass and doesn't apply inside the park). Standard NPS entrance fee applies: $30/vehicle (7 consecutive days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From the Fryingpan Creek Trailhead (~3,800 ft), about 2.9 mi past the White River entrance station on Sunrise/White River Road (WA-410), via the Wonderland Trail through Summerland

names: Dingford Creek / Middle Fork Snoqualmie Trailhead
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest / Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: No parking pass is required at this route's trailhead.
drive: From I-90 near North Bend, take exit 34, turn left onto 468th Street and follow it to Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road. Go 12 miles to the large Middle Fork parking area, pass it, and turn right onto a gravel road just after the large concrete bridge, signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap. Follow it 6 miles over potholes to a gate, with the trailhead just past it.

names: Pond pullout east of Washington Pass (SR-20)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to Burlington/Sedro-Woolley, then east on SR-20 through Marblemount and over Rainy Pass to Washington Pass; from Winthrop/Mazama it's a quick 20-30 minute drive west on SR-20 instead.
From I-90 take Exit 47 for Denny Creek and follow Forest Road 58 to the three Denny Creek parking lots, about half a mile past the campground (Northwest Forest Pass or Sno-Park permit).

names: Dutch Henry Falls trailhead pullout (Jameson Lake Road)
drive: From Wenatchee, drive east on US 2 past Waterville and Douglas and the junction with SR 182, then about 8 miles farther turn left on paved Jameson Lake Road; the north trailhead is about 4 miles along on the left, marked by a small preserve sign.

landManager: USDA Forest Service — Gifford Pinchot National Forest, Mount Adams Wilderness
storedPass: No trailhead parking pass is required at the Killen Creek Trailhead. The Mount Adams Climbing Pass applies separately above 7,000 ft.
drive: From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to the junction with FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground. Follow FR-2329 past the campground for about 4.5 miles to the trailhead.

names: Bird Creek Meadows (Yakama Nation, Mirror Lake road)
landManager: Yakama Nation (Yakama Indian Reservation, Tract D)
storedPass: Yakama tribal-use permit.
drive: From the gas station in Trout Lake, take the right fork north and follow the Mount Adams Recreation Area signs on the main road, which becomes Road 82, about 14.7 miles, past Mirror Lake; just past it take the left fork to the Bird Lake trailhead. The Yakama Nation closed the recreation area by order in August 2026 because of nearby fires, and it is open only part of the year, so confirm it is open before you go.

From Trout Lake, drive Mt. Adams Road north about 1.3 miles, then turn left onto Forest Road 23 (Buck Creek Road) and follow it about 17.5 miles to the trailhead, which is easy to miss between mileposts 38 and 37.

landManager: Gifford Pinchot National Forest (Mt. Adams Ranger District) — Mount Adams Wilderness
storedPass: Cold Springs/South Climb Trailhead day-use fee: $5/vehicle/day or $30/year (a Northwest Forest Pass satisfies this; the Climbing Pass’s parking stub also covers it May 1–Sept 30).
drive: From Trout Lake, drive Mount Adams Road north to the V intersection with FR-23, veer right and go about 1 mile, then turn left onto FR-80 (signed South Climb) and follow it to its end. Turn right onto FR-8040 and drive north past Morrison Creek Campground to the old Cold Springs Camp; the last 3 miles are very rough and narrow.

landManager: U.S. Forest Service
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From Trout Lake, drive north on Mount Adams Road to the V intersection with Forest Road 23, veer right and go about 1 mile, then turn left onto Forest Road 80 (signed South Climb) and follow it to its end. Turn right onto Forest Road 8040 and drive north past Morrison Creek Campground to the trailhead; the last 3 miles are very rough and narrow.

names: Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center (High Ridge Trail)
landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From US-101 in Port Angeles, head south on Race Street for 1.2 miles to Hurricane Ridge Road, then drive about 17.5 miles uphill to the visitor center lot.

landManager: U.S. Forest Service
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From SR-20 just past milepost 82, turn north onto Baker Lake Road and follow it about 12 miles, turn left onto FR-12, and after about 3.5 miles turn right onto FR-13, which runs to the trailhead parking at its end.

names: Little Giant Trailhead (Chiwawa River Road, Trail #1518)
landManager: Glacier Peak Wilderness, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Wenatchee River Ranger District (Leavenworth, WA)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / Interagency (America the Beautiful) Pass

landManager: U.S. Forest Service -- Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Glacier Peak Wilderness)
drive: From Marblemount, drive 14.2 miles up Cascade River Road and turn right onto FR-1570 (Kindy Creek Road) across the Kindy Creek bridge and about 2 miles up the rough spur to a small pullout near Vee Creek, about 1,850 ft.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Darrington Ranger District (Glacier Peak Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: The hike-in starts where FR-16 (Illabot Creek Road) reaches the Arrow Creek switchback (~2,220 ft) — this is the trailhead, not a formal one.

names: No separate trailhead — over Mount Crowder by its Southwest Route
landManager: North Cascades National Park Service Complex / Stephen Mather Wilderness (NPS)
storedPass: A Northwest Forest Pass may be required at some USFS trailheads used to approach the range; none needed inside the National Park.

names: Cathedral Rock / Deception Pass Trailhead (Tucquala Meadows)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Cle Elum Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: From Roslyn, follow SR 903 north about 14.8 miles to the end of the maintained road, bear right onto Forest Road 4330, and continue on gravel to the trailhead at its end.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Alpine Lakes Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / National Park Pass
drive: From the Deception Pass Trailhead

landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: None — the Thornton Lakes Trailhead lies inside North Cascades National Park, so no Northwest Forest Pass or NPS entrance fee applies; only the overnight wilderness permit above is required.
drive: Start at the Thornton Lakes Trailhead (~2,500 ft), reached via the rough spur road off SR-20 near milepost 117.

landManager: U.S. Forest Service — Olympic National Forest, Hood Canal Ranger District (Mount Skokomish Wilderness)
storedPass: $5/vehicle day-use fee or $30 annual Northwest Forest Pass required to park at the upper trailhead — Interagency/Digital Pass also accepted (cash not accepted on site); the lower trailhead is fee-free.
drive: From the Upper Trailhead (elev. ~3,500 ft, at the end of FS Road 2419-014 off FS 24/FS 2419 - the lot has a vault toilet, picnic table, and requires a Northwest Forest Pass), Trail #812 climbs immediately.

landManager: North Cascades National Park Service Complex (NPS)
Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: Start from the Bagley Lakes Trailhead (~4,200 ft) at the south end of the upper Mt. Baker Ski Area parking lot near the Heather Meadows Visitor Center.

names: North Fork Quinault Trailhead / Ranger Station
landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From US-101 at milepost 126, turn onto South Shore Road and follow it 12.9 miles to the Quinault River bridge; cross it, turn right onto North Shore Road, and drive 3.5 miles to the road end at the trailhead and ranger station.

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: None required at the Upper South Fork Skokomish trailhead, and there is no Olympic National Park entrance station on this approach.

landManager: Olympic National Forest (Hood Canal Ranger District), Mount Skokomish Wilderness
storedPass: No day-use fee at the Jefferson Creek/Jefferson Lake trailhead; a Northwest Forest Pass may be requested at some other nearby Olympic NF trailheads.
drive: From Hoodsport, drive about 14 miles north on US 101 to Hamma Hamma River Road (FR 25); follow it roughly 6.5 miles to FR 2480, then FR 2480 about 3 miles to FR 2401, then FR 2401 roughly 7-7.5 miles to the Jefferson Creek crossing / Jefferson Lake Trailhead area (~2,440 ft).

names: FR-6220 / Anderson Creek drainage (no maintained trail)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.

names: FR-62 road-end (~2,800 ft, off US-2 near Index)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: No federal pass needed at the FR-62 road-end pullout; the Hampton Resources recreation permit is what this approach requires.
drive: From US-2 near Index onto FR-62: left at both junctions, ~5 miles to the rough road-end and the West Ridge boot path

landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / Interagency Pass
drive: From the Verlot Public Service Center on the Mountain Loop Highway, continue east about 4.6 miles and turn right onto Forest Road 4020 (Schweitzer Creek Road, signed for Boardman Lake/Ashland Lakes/Bear-Pinnacle Lake).

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From Granite Falls, take Quarry Road about 4 miles to the Mountain Loop Highway, turn left and go 10 miles to Verlot, continue 1 mile and turn right onto Mount Pilchuck Road, then follow FR-42 for 6.8 miles to the trailhead lot.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From Darrington, turn right onto the Mountain Loop Highway and drive 12.5 miles to the signed turnoff on the left, then turn left onto FR-2095 and go 1.5 miles to the trailhead on the right.

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: Via the Elwha Valley: Olympic Hot Springs Road is closed to vehicles at Madison Falls — walk or bike ~6-7 miles to the Whiskey Bend Trailhead

names: Ruth Creek Road pullout near milepost 3 (FS 32)
landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mt. Baker Ranger District (Mount Baker Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency Pass
drive: From a pullout near milepost 3 on Ruth Creek Road, just past a creek flowing over a concrete weir (~2,950 ft), off Hannegan Pass Road (FS 32) from the Mt. Baker Highway

names: White Salmon Road (hairpin) TH / Lower White Salmon Lodge
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (approach) / National Park Service — North Cascades NP (upper mountain and summit)
storedPass: None required at the White Salmon Road pull-off; parking is very limited
drive: From the lower White Salmon lodge on SR-542 (White Salmon Road, FR-3075), via the old road into the White Salmon Creek drainage

names: White Salmon Lodge road gate (Mount Baker Highway hairpin)
landManager: National Park Service
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: At the hairpin on the Mount Baker Highway near mile 52, below the ski area, park in the small pull-off at the gated road to White Salmon Lodge. Don't block the gate.

landManager: U.S. Forest Service — Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument (Gifford Pinchot National Forest)
storedPass: $5/day/vehicle at Climber’s Bivouac, waived on the date of your climb with a valid climbing permit; any other day or night parked there needs the day fee or a Northwest Forest or Interagency pass.
drive: From the Climbers Bivouac trailhead (3,700 ft, the highest vehicle access on this side of the mountain, reached via FR-90/FR-83/FR-81/FR-830 from Cougar), the route starts on the signed Ptarmigan Trail #216A through open forest.

landManager: U.S. Forest Service — Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument (Gifford Pinchot National Forest)
storedPass: Washington Sno-Park permit to park at Marble Mountain Sno-Park during the winter Sno-Park season.
drive: From Cougar, drive east on Lewis River Road, which becomes Forest Road 90, to the junction with Forest Road 83; turn left and go about 6 miles to the Marble Mountain Sno-Park. Forest Road 83 is gated at the sno-park in winter and early spring.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From the Olney Creek Road gate

names: Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center / Hoh River Trailhead
landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From Forks, drive US-101 south about 13 miles and turn east onto Upper Hoh Road. Follow it about 18 miles to the visitor center and trailhead at the end of the road.

landManager: USDA Forest Service — Olympic National Forest (Buckhorn Wilderness)
storedPass: No fees; no Northwest Forest Pass or Discover Pass needed at either trailhead.
drive: Start at the Mt. Townsend Upper Trailhead (elev. ~3,300 ft), reached via Forest Road 27 off Penny Creek Road out of Quilcene - the trailhead has a small gravel lot and a Buckhorn Wilderness boundary sign where Trail #839 begins.

landManager: Olympic National Forest (Hood Canal Ranger District), Mount Skokomish Wilderness
Olympic National Forest — Buckhorn Wilderness, Hood Canal (Quilcene) Ranger District
storedPass: None required.
drive: Start at the Tubal Cain Trailhead (elev. ~3,300 ft, reached via FR 2870/2880), and follow the Tubal Cain Trail #840 (Copper Creek drainage) south.

landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mt. Baker Ranger District
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at the Cascade River Road trailhead/parking area
drive: Park at the Cascade River Road washout roughly 14.2 miles from Marblemount, about 100 yards past the Cascade River crossing near the FR 1570 junction (signed for Kindy Ridge/Found Lake).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Cle Elum Ranger District.
drive: Start at the Stafford Creek Trailhead (Trail #1359), Cle Elum Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, at the end of Stafford Creek Road (FR 9703), which leaves North Fork Teanaway River Road (FR 9737) past 29 Pines Campground - a small, often-overflowing lot for roughly 20 cars (Northwest Forest Pass required).

names: NF-9070 road-end below Silver Basin (Hyak, I-90 Exit 54)
landManager: USDA Forest Service — FR-9070 runs through the Cle Elum Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / America the Beautiful Pass (required at the FR-9070 PCT-crossing trailhead)
drive: From I-90 Exit 54 via Hyak Drive and NF-9070 (left fork at Ollallie Meadow) to the road-end turnaround

storedPass: N/A
drive: Drive to Tiffany Springs Campground (elev. ~6,760 ft) via Forest Road 39, accessed either from Conconully (south, via FR-37) or from Winthrop (southwest, via East Chewuch Road and FR-37) - both are long gravel-road drives of an hour or more.

landManager: Gifford Pinchot National Forest (Cowlitz Valley Ranger District) — Goat Rocks Wilderness
storedPass: Required at both the Snowgrass Flat and Berry Patch trailheads — $5/day or $30/year Northwest Forest Pass.
drive: From the Snowgrass Flats Trailhead (end of FR-2150, elev. ~4,600 ft), start on Trail 96 (Snowgrass Flat Trail).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District — Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency Recreation Pass (or pay the $5 day-use fee)
drive: Park at the Eagle Creek/Oval trailhead (~3,000 ft) at the end of FR 4420-080, reached via Twisp River Road/FR 44 (~12.5 mi west of Twisp) and the West Buttermilk/FR 4420 spur.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to Burlington/Sedro-Woolley, then east on SR-20 through Marblemount and over Rainy Pass to Washington Pass; from Winthrop/Mazama it's a quick 20-30 minute drive west on SR-20 instead.

names: Hannegan Pass Trailhead (end of Ruth Creek Rd / FR-32), via Hannegan Pass, Chilliwack River Trail, Whatcom Pass and Perfect Pass to the SW side of Phantom Peak
landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: None inside the park; a Northwest Forest Pass may be required at some adjacent national forest trailheads.
drive: From the Mount Baker Highway (SR-542), turn onto Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32) and drive 5.3 miles to the trailhead at the end of the road

landManager: National Park Service
storedPass: Not a Northwest Forest Pass (that's a USFS pass and doesn't apply inside the park). Standard NPS entrance fee applies: $30/vehicle (7 consecutive days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From Elbe, drive SR-706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance of the park, then continue about 6.5 miles to Longmire. The center is in the Longmire Administration Building, across from the museum.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Not needed at the SR-20 roadside pullout used for the Wine Spires. A Northwest Forest Pass is required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: East of Washington Pass on SR-20, pullout on right/south side of highway

names: PCT North Trailhead, Snoqualmie Pass (I-90 Exit 52)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District (within the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness)
drive: From the Reynolds Creek Trailhead (~3,100-3,170 ft, reached via Forest Road 4435, which crosses the Twisp River near Mystery Campground before the Spur 4435-015 turnoff to the trailhead), the route follows Reynolds Creek Trail #402, an unmaintained, primitive Forest Service trail entering the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District (Leavenworth, WA)
drive: Begin at the Old Merritt Lake Trailhead off US-2 (~2,950 ft).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District
storedPass: None at the primary US-2 trailhead; Northwest Forest Pass required at some alternate trailheads (e.g., Kahler Glen/Nason Ridge Trailhead).
drive: From the Rock Mountain Trail #1587 pullout on US-2 (small dirt lot on the north side of the highway near the powerlines, no facilities), the trail launches immediately uphill on what was formerly a service road.

landManager: Gifford Pinchot National Forest (USFS)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From Randle, drive south on Forest Road 25 to Forest Road 2551, just south of Elk Pass, then east on FR2551 for about 1.6 miles to an unmarked spur on the left; park at or just past the spur.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mount Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From Sedro-Woolley, drive WA-9 north to Acme, turn right (east) onto Mosquito Lake Road and follow it about 9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River and continue onto Forest Road 38 for about 11 miles to the Elbow Lake trailhead. Since July 2026 Forest Road 38 has been closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 7.
From Interstate 90 exit 52, turn onto State Route 906, then continue onto Erste Strasse (Alpental Access Road) and follow it for 1.1 miles to a left turn into the Alpental lots.

names: Dailey Prairie logging-road gate (Middle Fork Nooksack)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
storedPass: No developed fee trailhead here — FR 38 gate/pullout is an undeveloped roadside parking spot; no Northwest Forest Pass required.
drive: From the Middle Fork Nooksack bridge gate: bike the Dailey Prairie logging roads to the north-side climbers' paths (gate status changes year to year — verify before the trip)

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.
drive: Park at the Yodelin lot on US 2 (the former Yodelin ski area's lot, now used for overflow parking, roughly 1.7 miles from the Stevens Pass Ski Area pedestrian overpass, around milepost 60).

names: FR-63 roadside pullout east of Galena
landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Skykomish Ranger District (Wild Sky Wilderness)
storedPass: No pass needed at the FR-63 roadside pullout east of Galena.
drive: Drive US-2 to Skykomish, then north on Beckler River Road (FR-65) for about 15 miles; turn left (west) onto FR-63 and follow it about 4.6 miles to where it crosses the North Fork Skykomish River again; park at the unmarked pullout on the rise just past the bridge, about a mile east of Galena. Since the December 2025 floods Beckler River Road has been closed beyond Jack Pass and the North Fork Skykomish bridge on FR-63 is out, so this pullout cannot be reached by car right now.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District (Buttermilk Creek/Twisp approach); the Prince Creek/Chelan Summit Trail approach falls under the Chelan Ranger District on the Lake Chelan side.
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass (or America the Beautiful/Interagency Pass) required to park at the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trailhead.
drive: Trailhead is the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trailhead (Trail #411), reached via Twisp River Road ~10.7-10.8 miles from Twisp, then left on Buttermilk Creek Road, staying left onto East Buttermilk Road (Forest Road 43) for roughly 4 miles, then right onto the Road 500 spur for about 2.7 miles to the road-end trailhead at about 3,960 ft.
From Interstate 90 exit 52, turn onto State Route 906, then continue onto Erste Strasse (Alpental Access Road) and follow it for 1.1 miles to a left turn into the lot just below the main lodges.

landManager: North Cascades National Park (National Park Service)
storedPass: No federal recreation pass required for the park; backcountry permit required for overnight camping.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Alpine Lakes Wilderness (Middle Fork Snoqualmie side)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / Interagency pass
drive: From the drivable end of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (NF-56)

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful interagency pass to park at the Upper Dungeness Trailhead, which is on Olympic National Forest land.
drive: Drive Hwy 101 to just before Sequim Bay State Park, turn onto Louella Rd, then Palo Alto Rd (becomes FR 28) for about 6 miles, turn right on FR 2880 along the Dungeness River, then in 1.7 miles turn left on FR 2870 and continue roughly 6.5-9 miles (gravel, winds steeply down to a river crossing) to the large Dungeness/Royal Basin trailhead lot (picnic table, vault toilet).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District — within the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From the Foggy Dew Trailhead (3,400 ft)

landManager: Olympic National Park (National Park Service)
storedPass: NPS wilderness camping permit (Recreation.gov) required for overnight stays; a day climb does not need a wilderness permit but a park entrance fee/pass applies.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
drive: Head northwest from the Mazama store on Lost River Road for 1.5 miles and pull into the big lot on the right-hand side. The lot is on private land that climbers may use by permission, so do not camp there.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.
drive: From Skykomish, drive US-2 east about 12 miles; just as the highway crests a deep curve over Tunnel Creek, turn right onto FR-6095 (possible only from the eastbound lane) and go about 1.3 miles to the trailhead.

landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District) — Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From Skykomish, drive US-2 east about 10 miles to an unsigned right turn near milepost 58.7, just past the old railroad community of Scenic; cross the railroad tracks, turn right, and follow the narrow dirt road about 0.3 mile to the trailhead.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From Glacier, drive east on Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) for about 12 miles and turn left onto Twin Lakes Road (FR 3065) at the end of the maintenance facility. Follow it about 4.5 miles to the trailhead parking.

names: Unsigned climbers' path off FS Road 56
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.

drive: From South Canyon Road in Ellensburg, drive Umtanum Road about 10 miles southwest to the trailhead.
From Enumclaw drive SR 410 east toward Crystal Mountain to the signed Skookum Falls viewpoint pullout on the right, about 9.5 miles south of Greenwater.

landManager: North Cascades National Park (NPS); trailhead access via Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass required at the Hannegan Trailhead
drive: From Bellingham, drive SR-542 east about 46 miles, which is 13 miles past Glacier, and just before the third crossing of the Nooksack River turn left onto FR-32, then follow it 5.3 miles to its end at Hannegan Campground, where the trailhead is.
From White Pass drive east on US 12 for about 2.2 miles to Dog Lake and park near it; the Clear Creek Falls overlook lot is likely snowed in during winter.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From SR-530 at Whitehorse, about 5 miles west of Darrington, turn left (south) onto Old Mine Road (387th Ave NE) at the gas station and drive 0.6 miles to the dead end.

landManager: Colville National Forest, Tonasket Ranger District (Pasayten Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / America the Beautiful Pass
drive: From Loomis, take County Road #9425 north 2 miles to County Road #4066/FR-39; follow FR-39 about 14 miles, then turn onto FR-3900-500 and follow it about 6 miles (high-clearance vehicle recommended, not advised for passenger cars) to the Iron Gate Trailhead.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Pasayten Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at the Long Swamp trailhead — $5/day or $30/annual.
